subject: I can do this in plot. How to do it in ggplot?

messages.author: 62f725013dca6cda
messages.subject: I can do this in plot. How to do it in ggplot?
parts:
Folks,
  My data is simple:

scaled.df<-structure(list(pcts = c(0, 0.067, 0.134, 0.201, 0.268, 0.335, 
0.402, 0.469, 0.536, 0.603, 0.67), counts = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 
0.19047619047619, 0, 0.0476190476190476, 0.0952380952380952, 
0.0952380952380952, 0.571428571428571)), .Names = c("pcts", "counts"
), row.names = c(NA, -11L), class = "data.frame")


This works for me:
qplot(counts, data = scaled.df, geom="density", xlim=c(0,1))

How do I accomplish the same thing in ggplot?

Thanks for your time,
KW


--

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: I can do this in plot. How to do it in ggplot?
parts:
Do you understand that qplot is part of ggplot--a "quick-plot"
facility? You're not using base graphics there.

But using the ggplot command, you could do this:

>ggplot(scaled.df, aes( counts ) ) + geom_density() + scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1))

Ben
